B1.name: fail whole
B1.publication: one archive of every file, or nothing
B1.failurePropagation: the first FAILED file stops the batch; files after it are CANCELLED unrun; nothing is published
B1.manifest: none: nothing is published when anything fails

B2.name: explicit partial
B2.publication: one archive of the SUCCEEDED files plus a manifest
B2.failurePropagation: none: a FAILED file is recorded and the batch continues
B2.manifest: always, in the archive and on screen: every file, its PLAN, its FileResult, and why

B3.name: independent jobs
B3.ownership: one owner per file, under a batch owner that can cancel every file not yet published
B3.publication: one artifact per SUCCEEDED file, no archive
B3.downloadTiming: as soon as each file succeeds
B3.cancellation: per file; cancelling the batch cancels the files not yet published
B3.manifest: none: each file carries its own state

lines.name: H1 Monochrome: is intentional rasterisation acceptable, or is a structure-preserving implementation required?
lines.detail: recommendation: Keep rasterisation (candidate A) for the M5 MVP only as an explicit INTENTIONAL_FLATTENING operation whose PLAN names every loss and requires confirmation; take candidate C (structure-preserving, fail-closed) forward as a separate spike measured on real drawings before it is offered. Note H8: with the browser encoder, no hard memory guarantee exists for the rasterising path today.

lines.name: H2a Optimize — meaning: what does 「最適化」 promise (O1 flatten / O2 lossless / O3 preservation levels), and may O1 keep that name?
lines.detail: recommendation: O1 must not keep the name: measured, it removes all text and structure and makes vector drawings 11-153x larger at its default and up to 463x. O2 (lossless, never larger) is the floor 「最適化」 can promise today; whether it also means O3 depends on H2b.

lines.name: H2b Optimize — lossy contract for O3: target-DPI semantics, JPEG quality, whether lossy recompression is acceptable at all, raster linework / scanned-text quality, and skip-versus-recompress.
lines.detail: recommendation: Measured on a 300 dpi one-pixel linework scan: resampling to 150 dpi keeps only ~22-26% of the line ink whether lossless or JPEG; JPEG q0.8 at the scan's own resolution keeps 100% at x0.33. Recommended if adopted: never resample below the source resolution without an explicit per-run choice; JPEG only when smaller; quality >= 0.8; everything else skipped and reported.

lines.name: H3 Margin: which source structure must survive?
lines.detail: recommendation: Adopt the in-place transform with its exact contract: text, OCR, vectors, raster bytes, annotations (moved), links and their destinations (XYZ/Fit*/FitR, named, outlines — moved with their target page), form widgets and values (with /DA and border scaled), XFA, metadata, /Rotate and CropBox all survive; refused before any change: q/Q underflow, unknown annotation types, annotations not wholly inside the visible page, destinations of unknown type or into no page of the document, structure destinations, GoToE.

lines.name: H4 Batch failure: B1 fail whole, B2 explicit partial with a manifest, or B3 independent per-file jobs (one download per file, as each finishes)?
lines.detail: recommendation: B2 — one archive after the last file, the successes plus a manifest naming every file's PLAN, FileResult and reason, also on screen. Today's partial ZIP carries no record of the failure.

lines.name: H5 Searchable text / OCR: may an intentionally flattening operation remove it, and on what confirmation?
lines.detail: recommendation: Only with an explicit per-run confirmation that names the loss; never as a default and never silently.

lines.name: H6 Annotations and forms: preserve, refuse, or explicitly flatten — per operation?
lines.detail: recommendation: Structure-preserving operations preserve and transform them within the stated contract or refuse by name; flattening operations list them among the confirmed losses. An empty signature field is a form field for this purpose (see H7).

lines.name: H7 Signatures and XFA. For signatures there are two coherent rules: (A) refuse an *applied* signature — a /Sig field whose /V holds a signature dictionary — and treat an empty /Sig field as a form object; or (B) refuse any signature infrastructure at all, including an empty field or /SigFlags alone. Which rule, and does it cover the hardened lanes? Separately, which XFA rule: refuse always, refuse only where it is dropped, or confirm where it is dropped?
lines.detail: recommendation: A, plus 'refuse-if-dropped' for XFA — the policy named 'applied-only'. An applied signature cannot survive any operation here (all re-serialise), so it is refused for every operation, the hardened lanes included. An empty /Sig field has nothing to invalidate: measured, Layer keeps it and Monochrome removes it with the rest of the form, so it belongs to that operation's form contract (H6) and not to a signature refusal. /SigFlags alone is recorded as a fact and refuses nothing under A. Choose B only if the product wants signable documents kept away from the Processor entirely; it would refuse documents that merely contain a blank signature box.

lines.name: H8 Memory for the flattening operations: default and explicit override — BLOCKED, pending a Raster Encoder / Memory Sub-Spike.
lines.detail: recommendation: Do not adopt a hard operation-memory budget in this round. The pipeline's own buffers are exact or source-derived, but the browser JPEG encoder is not owned: neither its encoded size nor its internal working memory can be bounded from any implementation this research controls. Measured compression ratios are performance evidence, not a safety proof. Under the only fail-closed JPEG term available (the format's own 20 B/px entropy-coding bound) the flattening operations barely fit at 512 MiB — see measurements.md — which is itself the argument for the sub-spike: an owned encoder (the repository already owns an exact-size PNG encoder from M4) or a bounded encoding path would make this decidable. Until then 512 MiB remains a candidate, not a guarantee, and the 'planning' numbers must be labelled as estimates.

lines.name: H9 Raster resolution: which DPI are offered, and how is an impossible one refused without a silent downgrade?
lines.detail: recommendation: Adoptable now, independently of H8: MAX_RASTER_PIXELS 134,217,728 (128 Mi px) as the portable policy ceiling — below the 139-279 Mpx boundary measured on one machine, not that boundary itself — plus a runtime canvas-allocation probe before each page that refuses if it fails. Both are computed from pixel counts the architecture owns. The UI keeps its options; the preflight refuses with the numbers (A0 at 300 dpi, A1 and A0 at 600 dpi) and never lowers the DPI.

lines.name: H10 Cancellation: atomic output and ownership — does a settings change, file change or navigation supersede a run?
lines.detail: recommendation: Yes: the F1-B/M4 owner token, captured at start and re-read at every file boundary and immediately before each publish; unmount, a settings change and a file-list change supersede. Under B3 a file's own change supersedes that file only.

lines.name: H11 Common Processor orchestration: one PLAN/RESULT engine, or per-tool engines?
lines.detail: recommendation: One orchestration (SourceFacts, the H7 policy, the raster preflight, ownership, the batch policy, publish) with per-operation planners and runners; the hardened lanes enter it unchanged behind the common facts step.

lines.name: H12 Metadata: which operations may change the Info dictionary and XMP, and must a flattening operation carry them into the new document?
lines.detail: recommendation: No operation changes metadata silently: preserve Info/XMP (load with updateMetadata: false; copy them into rebuilt documents) unless the Human Gate names a change.

lines.name: H13a Layer extent: does the overlay cover the visible page (CropBox ∩ MediaBox) or the MediaBox from (0,0)?
lines.detail: recommendation: The visible page, in the page's own coordinates; today it misses 61% of the ink when the MediaBox does not start at the origin.

lines.name: H13b Layer stacking: does the overlay sit below annotations (as today) or above them?
lines.detail: recommendation: Measured: today the overlay is below every annotation (content stream), with no rewriting. 'Above' is possible without flattening only as one more annotation painted last — it then is an annotation itself (selectable, deletable, printed by its /F flag). Recommend below, stated in the UI; 'above' only if the Human Gate accepts an overlay annotation.
